China is seeing a historic boom in exports due to AI.

China’s exports rose +25% YoY in August, their 3rd-largest monthly reading in at least 2 years.

At the same time, imports surged +28%, pushing the monthly trade surplus to +$119 billion and the year-to-date surplus to +$806 billion.

This puts China’s trade surplus on track for another annual record, following the $1.2 trillion seen in 2025.

This all comes as high-tech exports contributed more than half of China’s export growth last month.

Integrated-circuit shipments soared +130% YoY in August, while high-tech product exports jumped +57%.

The AI boom is increasingly powering China’s export engine.

BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +78.3% YoY in the first 20 days of September, its strongest monthly growth on record.

This brought the value of exports to $71.4 billion, an all-time high.

This also marks the 5th consecutive month with growth of at least +50.0%.

Furthermore, exports adjusted for working-day differences rose +89.8% YoY, following a +61.5% increase during the same period in August.

Semiconductor exports were the key driver, surging +259.4% YoY to a record $34.1 billion.

Shipments to the US jumped +118.0% while shipments to China rose +113.8%, 

South Korea has become an economic powerhouse.

tweets.text:
The US 5-year Treasury yield just breached 5% for the first time since 2007.

That is the year before the money printing began. An entire generation of investors has never seen the cost of money this high. The Fed hiked again last week, its first hike since 2023, and traders are betting on more.

This is the number that matters, because almost everything prices off the 5-year. Mortgages, corporate debt, and stock valuations all discount against it. When the risk-free rate resets to a 19-year high, every risk asset has to clear a taller bar. The bond market is done lending cheap to a government that keeps spending, and stocks have not repriced for it yet.

🇪🇺 In August, registrations of fully electric cars jumped by more than 50% year-on-year across Europe (+75% in Germany and more than +100% in France). 

📈 Since the start of the year, EV market share had already been rising sharply thanks to several factors such as more models in the €20,000-25,000 range, better driving ranges, more charging infrastructure and still very significant government support. Oil is not creating the trend but it is hitting at a point where the market was already close to a tipping point and is now accelerating the move dramatically.

🤷‍♂️ Meanwhile, this EV boom can be great news for Europe’s energy transition while becoming bad news for Europe’s auto industry at the same time. Chinese manufacturers are very well positioned in this market with competitive vehicles, highly integrated supply chains and aggressive pricing, and their market share in Europe is approaching 12% in some months. Europe spent years pushing the auto industry toward electrification, and now that the transition is finally accelerating, the companies best positioned to benefit from it are not necessarily European. Quite a paradox, ain't it ?

Oil probably did not trigger Europe’s EV boom but it may simply turn a gradual transition into a much more abrupt acceleration.

*Bloomberg link: https://t.co/jaeIrkmjZy

The Bank of Japan raised rates to the highest level since 1995, and the yen fell.

The hike was 25 basis points to 1.25%, but two board members voted against it and Governor Ueda refused to sound hawkish. Traders read that as Japan blinking. The yen slid to 157 per dollar, back toward the weak end of its range.

Here is what actually matters. Even after the hike, Japan's rate sits far below the US, so the yen carry trade stays alive. That is cheap Japanese money still funding risk bets around the world. It works until Japan is forced to close the gap. When that carry trade unwinds, the selling travels straight to US stocks.

Bitcoin broke through the May high this week, which I clearly got wrong. I thought that energy/yields/rates heading higher would immediately pressure Bitcoin.

A weekly close above the May high would improve confidence in the rally.

The long end rising recently is starting to pressure risk assets. So far, Bitcoin has shrugged it off, which caught me off guard.

If that changes, and Bitcoin closes back below the range highs with this move ending up as just a wick, things can change quickly.

I'm trying to be less deterministic about these outcomes. The rally above the May high certainly humbled me.

For breakout traders, I think the weekly candle is worth watching closely for either confirmation of the breakout or a failed move back into the range, particularly with rates rising into a supply shock.

I discussed this at length in my last video for anyone curious about a more serious discussion rather than just a brief post.

Good Morning from Germany, where the economy is defying surging energy prices & higher interest rates. Ifo business confidence rose for a 5th straight month to 89.9 in Sep, beating expectations of 89.0. 
Both current conditions and expectations improved as spending on defence and infrastructure starts reaching the economy. Yet all 3 gauges remain well below their long-term averages. A cyclical rebound is taking shape; a structural comeback still needs reforms. 
Taken at face value, the Ifo reading points to GDP growth of ~0.5% QoQ in Q3, acc to Capital Economics; though it doubts actual growth will be that strong.
